conscription.note: Manpower is the share of the population of controlled provinces that can be called up. The peace multiplier prices raising the law while not at war. Happiness is the peacetime figure, halved at war and falling to nothing as the country is occupied.

options.name: Volunteer only
options.description: Only those who come forward are taken.

options.name: Limited conscription
options.description: A lottery takes a small intake each year.

options.name: Extensive conscription
options.description: Every man fit for service serves a term.

options.name: Service by requirement
options.description: Men are conscripted on demand without exemption.

options.name: Total mobilisation
options.description: Women are conscripted and the age limit widens.

economy.note: Consumer share is the share of civilian factories making goods for the population and taking no state orders. It is multiplied by the holding ideology's modifier. Conversion is days per factory changed between civilian and military. The peace multiplier prices raising the law while not at war.

options.name: Civilian economy
options.description: Industry produces for civilian demand.

options.name: Early mobilisation
options.description: Civilian factories begin taking military orders.

options.name: Partial mobilisation
options.description: State demands are prioritised ahead of civilian ones.

options.name: War economy
options.description: The state controls what every factory produces.

options.name: Total war
options.description: Everything except essential services is directed to war.

personalTax.note: Revenue is the multiplier on the population term of provincial tax.

options.name: Minimal taxation
options.description: Income is barely taxed.

options.name: Low taxation
options.description: Income is taxed at a low rate, with wide exemptions.

options.name: Moderate taxation
options.description: Income is taxed at an ordinary rate.

options.name: High taxation
options.description: Income is taxed at a high rate.

options.name: Punitive taxation
options.description: Income is taxed at a confiscatory rate.

corporateTax.note: Revenue is the multiplier on the factory term of provincial tax.

options.name: Minimal taxation
options.description: Profits are barely taxed.

options.name: Low taxation
options.description: Profits are taxed at a low rate.

options.name: Moderate taxation
options.description: Profits are taxed at an ordinary rate.

options.name: High taxation
options.description: Profits are taxed at a high rate.

options.name: Punitive taxation
options.description: Profits are taxed to the point of deterring investment.

colonialTax.note: Applies to provinces of colonies. A polity holding none omits the law entirely. Colonial unrest is a figure a day added in every colonial province.

options.name: Minimal taxation
options.description: The colonies retain most of their revenue.

options.name: Low taxation
options.description: The colonies remit a small portion of their revenue.

options.name: Moderate taxation
options.description: The colonies remit the customary portion of their revenue.

options.name: High taxation
options.description: The colonies remit most of their revenue.

options.name: Punitive taxation
options.description: The colonies remit all revenue above their administrative costs.

monetary.note: Loosening the anchor takes changeDays and tightening it takes tightenDays. Interest multiplies the debt * 0.0002 charged under Treasury. Debt thresholds multiplies where the four ratio penalties fall, so ×0.5 brings them at half the debt. Anything else carrying either multiplies the law figure rather than replacing it. The ladder runs tightest to loosest in the order below.

options.name: Gold standard
options.description: The currency is convertible to gold at a fixed rate.

options.name: Devalued parity
options.description: The currency is convertible to gold at a reduced parity.

options.name: Managed currency
options.description: The currency is not convertible and the state sets the rate.

options.name: Currency expansion
options.description: The state prints money to cover its own spending.

trade.note: Surplus offered is the share of a surplus put on the automatic market and deficit filled the share of a deficit the market may fill. Tariff ceiling is the highest rate the country may charge a foreign flag.

options.name: Free trade
options.description: Merchants buy and sell without restriction.

options.name: Export focus
options.description: Exports are favoured, and what comes the other way is taxed at the border.

options.name: Limited exports
options.description: Exports are limited by quota.

options.name: Closed economy
options.description: The borders are closed to private trade.

doctrine.note: One school per branch, held separately, in four branches: land, air, naval and magical. A country begins with the doctrine its history gives it and most never change. Land dragons take the land schools inside their divisions and a dragon squadron takes the air schools, with strategic bombing at half effect and double anti-air fire.

land.name: Mobile warfare
land.description: Armour is concentrated to break through and exploit the gap.

land.name: Superior firepower
land.description: Artillery and materiel are spent over manpower.

land.name: Mass assault
land.description: Infantry in numbers takes the place of armour and artillery.

land.name: Defensive
land.description: Entrenched positions are favoured over offensives.

air.name: Air superiority
air.description: Fighters clear the sky before any other aerial operations.

air.name: Battlefield support
air.description: Ground support is favoured over winning in the air or striking industry.

air.name: Strategic bombing
air.description: Bombing of industry and bases is prioritised.

air.name: Communications strike
air.description: Roads, railways and columns behind the enemy's front are struck before anything else.
air.special: Applies in any province within range of an air base of the polity or of an ally.

naval.name: Fleet in being
naval.description: Concentration of the capital fleet comes before all other tasks.
naval.special: The figure applies only to a capital ship with more than 2 escorts in its subregion or in one adjacent to it. An escort is a light cruiser, destroyer or submarine of the polity or of an ally.

naval.name: Convoy interdiction
naval.description: Sinking the enemy's supply convoys comes before fleet action.

naval.name: Trade interdiction
naval.description: Closing the enemy's shipping routes are prioritised over fleet action.
naval.special: A sea route is normally closed through any region an enemy controls. On this doctrine, a fleet blocks every enemy trade route regardless of regional strength.

naval.name: Base strike
naval.description: Striking enemy ships in harbour is favoured over meeting them at sea.

magical.name: Warded lines
magical.description: Runes are cut into the armour and into the fortifications along the whole front.

magical.name: Advanced legilimency
magical.description: Officers are trained to read the enemy and to keep their own minds closed.

magical.name: Wizard corps
magical.description: The country's wizards are gathered into one corps and set on what the enemy has built.
magical.special: Drawn from souls and not from crystal, so it consumes no tazkuri. What limits it is how few wizards are born.

magical.name: Gem ordnance
magical.description: Crystals are fired as incendiary shot, in the manner of the Khorshite pot.
magical.special: Burns 0.5 tazkuri a day for every division in combat, on top of any enchantment. A country that runs dry loses the figure until it is in supply again.
